en: The Ritual Manual for the Recitation and Practice of Samantabhadra from the *Tattvapatala* of the *Vajraśekhara-yoga-paranirmitavaśavartin-samādhi*, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master and Śramaṇa [Amoghavajra],
who held the rank of Special Advancement (Tejin) and Acting Minister of State Ceremonial (Shi Honglu Qing) during the Tang Dynasty.
Having purified my three karmas for the sake of benefiting all sentient beings so that they may attain the three bodies,
I take refuge and pay homage to the Three Jewels,
whose vajra body, speech, and mind pervade the entirety of saṃsāra.
Secret Vajradhātu, the protector who relies on great compassion, the heroic Akṣobhya;
the most supreme Ratnasaṃbhava, the compassionate Amitābha; and he who accomplishes unerring activity.
To all these Unsurpassed Honored Ones, I prostrate with my head bowed;
And to the Sattvavajra, the Supreme Victorious One who Subdues All,
The Treasury of Space, who is able to bestow all empowerments.
To the Savior Avalokiteśvara, To Viśvakarman, skilled in the yoga of the manifestation of samādhi,
And to all these noble deities who skillfully employ secret expedients— I prostrate myself before them all.
One who practices this dharma shall always abide in the contemplative practice of the *iṣṭadevatā* and tread upon lotus flowers.
Upon reaching the door of the meditation chamber, one snaps the fingers and utters "HŪṂ" three times;
then, one places the syllable MA upon the right eye.
Place the syllable *Ṭha* on the left eye; from the right sun and the left moon, vajra-light radiates and disperses.
Entering the gate and looking back, all māras are utterly dispersed. [Perform this] with the left vajra-fist.
Raising the index finger of the left hand upright, do the same with the right;
rotate three times counter-clockwise above the crown of the head, pointing toward space and the lower realms,
then rotate clockwise once more, reciting the *hūṃ* mantra throughout.
Next, contemplate that the Buddha is eternally present. Having performed prostrations to the Triple Gem, one then recites the *Vimalaprabhā* mantra.
With the two hands in the unopened lotus gesture, the secret meaning of this mantra is as follows: "The intrinsic nature of all phenomena is pure."
I too am pure by nature; through this empowerment, both self and others attain stainlessness.
Then, visualizing within one's own mind that the nature has become vajra, the three karmas have undergone transformation.
To accomplish the three gates of secrecy, next perform the mudrā of awakening:

with the two fists, join the *tarjanī* (forefinger) and *madhyamā* (middle finger) like hooks; extend the *tarjanī* and *anāmikā* (ring finger), supporting them side by side, and raise them in the gesture of a hook. Recite these secret words.
Through the empowerment of this seal of true speech, all Buddhas—who do not crave the flavor of quiescence—arise from their meditative absorptions and proceed to the assembly.
Having observed the practitioner and accepted them together, one next binds the Great Seal of Vajradhara:
cross the fingers of the left hand (dāna) and right hand (prajñā), and the thumbs (dhyāna) and index fingers (jñāna).

Placing the right knee on the ground and resting it upon the crown of the head, one should visualize the body filling the ocean of all dust-mote worlds and pay homage at the feet of each and every Tathāgata.
The mantra is as follows: "By means of this holding of the vajra seal, all Perfectly Awakened Ones shall accord with [the practitioner]."
Desiring to serve all Tathāgatas, one offers up the body to Akṣobhya Buddha;
with vajra-palms joined and raised above the crown of the head, the entire body is cast upon the ground in mental prostration.
The mantra is as follows:
By means of this mantra and body-mudrā, one immediately attains the perfection of bodhicitta.
Next, one should pay homage to the Honored One Ratnasambhava;
to receive the empowerment and its associated objects, one should join the vajra-palms at the heart and offer by placing the forehead upon the ground.
The mantra says:
"By virtue of this offering of the body, one immediately attains the rank of a Dharma King through empowerment;
desiring to entreat him to turn the wheel of Dharma, one offers the body as an offering to Amitāyus."
Placing the vajra-palms upon the crown of the head, touch the mouth to the ground and offer one’s body.
The mantra is as follows:
By means of requesting through this mantra, one immediately attains the wisdom that turns the sublime wheel of Dharma.
Next, one should pay homage to Amogharāja for the sake of seeking the *karmaprasādhana* rite;
with vajra-palms joined at the heart and the crown of the head touching the ground,
one should supplicate with this mantra:
Through this offering of one’s body and sincere entreaty, one is able to manifest various forms.
Next, visualize oneself before an ocean of Buddhas, performing repentance and making requests at the appropriate times.
Proceeding thus according to the *Laghu-yoga*, one immediately enters the samaya of the deity.
Sitting cross-legged with the body upright, one enters meditative absorption (*samādhi*).

One cultivates and applies the four immeasurable minds (*catur-apramāṇa*) throughout the entire dharma-realm according to the Dharma teachings. The mantra of Great Compassion (*mahāmaitrī*) is as follows:
When reciting this mantra, one extends the mind to pervade the three realms.
The Great Compassion Mantra for Universally Bestowing Happiness upon Sentient Beings is as follows:
When reciting this mantra, one’s mind pervades the realm of sentient beings to provide universal salvation. The Great Joy Mantra is as follows:
Having rescued each according to their kind, I empower all classes of sentient beings with this light;
having bestowed such benefit and bliss as enlightenment upon them all,
I then return to the nature of the dharmadhātu.
The mantra of great equanimity is as follows:
When reciting this mantra, the mind abides in equality, seeing neither self nor other;
there is only this single nature and characteristic.
This is the nature of Samantabhadra, the Great Bodhicitta.
Next, one should perform a circular dance with both hands and form the Vajra-joined-palms mudrā.
The first part of the ten [mudrās] is the Interlocking [Mudrā].
The mantra is: Oṃ vairocani. With this seal, one performs a firm binding;
it is named the Supreme Vajra Binding.
The mantra from which all mudrās arise is: Oṃ vajra-bandha.
Then, with the wisdom-finger (tarjanī) and the middle finger (madhyamā), enter the full moon;
place the forefinger (tarjanī) and the ring finger (anāmikā) upon its back.
The name is "Great Vajramuṣṭi.
The mantra of the Samaya-mudrā is:
Oṃ vajramuṣṭi maṃ. Then, it is divided into two.
The mantra for the samaya-mudrā of the *iṣṭadevatā* is as follows:
As soon as one binds the seal of the original vow and recites the mantra, one’s body comes to abide within a solar disc, identical to the *iṣṭadevatā*.
Next, one presents the mudrā of joyful delight (*pramuditā-samaya*), which causes all the noble ones to rejoice.
The binding mudrā with the thumbs and ring fingers joined, the palms full like the moon; the giving and wisdom hands, the meditation and insight hands, joined and held upright.
The mantra is as follows:
Next, one should open the gate of the heart and visualize the two breasts above.
To the right, *tra*; to the left, *ṭha*. With the three-fold vajra-bind, one should place it at the heart like opening a door. The mantra is as follows:
Visualize in the space of one cubit before you the syllable *aḥ*, white in color and radiant.
With meditative concentration and wisdom, place the hands in the moon-palms;
with the power of progress, join the two fingers at the second joint to seal the gate of the heart-palace within the mind.
The mantra for settling the mind is as follows: using the aforementioned fist-seal mudrā, seal the gates of the heart-palace.
Divide into two parts before the heart. Recite *HŪṂ* and raise the right hand;
then recite *HŪṂ* and raise the left in the same manner. With three *HŪṂ*s, hook them together;
with *HŪṂ*, extend the arms with force. Turning to the left, lead the way and perform the ritual expulsion.
Turning to the right, one forms the boundary; when performing this rite,
one dwells within a mind of great compassion while externally manifesting great wrath—
tearing forth sharp fangs on all four sides and wielding sharp weapons with eight arms.
With fierce flames erupting from his entire body, he assumes the posture of a great roar;
the assembly of Guhyaka Vajras stands in attendance, having received their instructions.
Next, one binds the Lotus Samaya: with the hands in the fundamental bind, the thumbs and wisdom-fingers are extended upward.
By means of this mantra and mudrā, the cultivation of samādhi will swiftly manifest.
The mantra is as follows:
Next, eliminate the peripheral movements of the mind and cause it to return to the wisdom of equality.
With the previous mudrā, join the *tarjanī* and *madhyamā* fingers;
then, with the final syllable of the mantra, suddenly pull apart the secret mudrā. The mantra is as follows:
As soon as this vidyā-mudrā is performed, the followers of the Two Vehicles are moved to compassion and rescue [beings].
Ordinary beings enter the Buddha-realm, and Buddhas appear to deliver sentient beings—
all is due to this empowerment. The mantra for attaining the mind of Samantabhadra is as follows:
By virtue of these mantras, all abide in the mind of great compassion;
both noble and ordinary beings alike receive joy.
This is called the Great Invitation of the Ordinary, which twice summons the karma produced by deluded views since beginningless time.
Bind with patience and aspiration like a needle; advance with vigor and power like a hook.
Visualize summoning all sins; the forms of these sinful hungry ghosts are reversed as seals toward the heart to summon them. Recite these words of truth.
From these three secret gates, all the karma of oneself and others is gathered;
it is called the *huṃ* of advancing power and support. This rope is drawn into the palms;
reciting *maṃ*, the fingers are interlaced, and the two pairs are hooked together in a knot.
Having bound all sinful karmas, extend the hands of patience and aspiration like banners;
with the syllable *buddhaṭṭa*, visualize them as vajra-clubs and strike them together as if crushing mountains— this is the wrathful phrase and the furious form.
It can purify all evil realms. Recite the mantra of the vidyā, patience, and aspiration three or seven times while snapping the fingers.
By means of this method of union, the sins accumulated through the three karmas— [are purified].
Having utterly destroyed these most heavy obstructions from beginningless time—
like a kalpa-fire consuming dry grass, sesame seeds, and the like—
the Tathāgata, out of his great compassion, has opened this most secret door.
Next, bind the secret mudrā: by dispersing and destroying the wheel of karmic obstructions, one accomplishes the buddha-activities.
With the vajra-anjali, bend the index and middle fingers back and join them;
press the ring and little fingers against their sides.
The mantra says:
In order to manifest one’s own intrinsic nature, One should employ the Lotus Samādhi Seal;
Through empowerment by this dharma, The three poisons will all be completely eliminated.
One's own mind as Great Bodhi is then accomplished.
Next, one enters the meditative absorption of the Wisdom of Wondrous Observation (*pratyavekṣaṇājñāna*). Forming the *baddhamudrā*, place it facing upward upon the *paryaṅka*;
join the tips of the thumbs and the index fingers, with the middle fingers crossed behind them. Press the index fingers against the thumbs.
This is called the Seal of the King Avalokiteśvara: Sit upright with the body straight and motionless;
Rest the tongue against the upper palate and keep the lips and teeth closed.
With the mind abiding in the great emptiness free from discrimination, The Buddhas fill the sky and come to awaken you, Declaring: "You have realized the purity of the One Way."
Until one has realized the Vajrayoga-samādhi, one should prostrate at the feet of the Buddha while in meditative absorption;
the remainder of the text is to be understood extensively according to what is taught in the *Yogācārabhūmi-śāstra*.
One should recite this mantra.
From the syllable *e* previously visualized within the heart, immeasurable red light radiates forth;
revolving to the right, it forms the sun. The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ citrapratiṣṭheṇa karomi. By the empowerment of this mantra, one's own mind is like the sun;
yet, because it has not yet become clear, [it remains obscured].
Furthermore, recite this mantra:
Oṃ bodhicittam utpādayāmi. By the empowerment of this mantra, it is like the orb of the sun in the height of summer.
The light shines brilliantly; then,
within the solar disc, one visualizes a white lotus flower and places the seed-syllable of the Honored One at its center.
The original light-color is white.
To accomplish the seal of the Honored One,
the mantra of Vajrajñāna is as follows:
Having empowered one's own mind with clarity through this mantra, *Oṃ tiṣṭha vajra yūyaḥ*,
one should again recite this mantra as follows:
Oṃ vajratma jñāṃ. The secret meaning of this is:
"I am the Vajra," that is, the Vajra formed by the three karmas.
Furthermore, one says, "I am a vajra-body.
When performing this contemplation,
this vajra extends throughout the entire dharma-realm.
All Buddhas enter this vajra and become one unified body. Furthermore,
the mantra for empowerment that makes it firm is as follows:
Oṃ nṛtye ṣṭha vajra. By this empowerment, one becomes extremely firm and immovable;
one then knows for oneself that one has attained the indestructible body of Vajra.
To accomplish the body of the *iṣṭadevatā*, one recites this mantra:
Oṃ atha karmakulodgata-sattva hūṃ. Next, [one recites] the mantra of the previously mentioned *samaya-mudrā* of the *iṣṭadevatā*.
Empower the heart, forehead, throat, and crown of the head.
Next, perform the empowerment rite:
place the Vajradhātveśvarī mudrā upon the crown of the head.
Next, for the mantra on the forehead, starting from the right and proceeding to the left, it is:
Oṃ Vajrasattva. Next, for the jewel on the crown, it is:
Oṃ Vajraratna. Next, for the dharma [wheel] at the back, it is: [Oṃ Vajradharma].
Oṃ vajradharma-carya. Oṃ vajrakarma-mudrā.
Form the basic binding with the thumbs and ring fingers like a sword.
The power of progress is attached to this.
Having been empowered by this,
the crowns of the five Tathāgatas rest upon his head.
Then, forming two fists,
bring them to the crown of the head; subsequently, exerting force, circle them three times,
and finally lower them to disperse while maintaining the posture of hanging silk streamers.
This is called the garland consecration (*mālābhiṣeka*).
It constitutes having already bound the stainless silk ribbon (*vimalapaṭṭa*).
The mantra is: Oṃ vajramale abhiṣiñca māṃ. Then, form two fists with both hands.
Exerting the power of effort,
visualize the syllable Oṃ on the surface of the Effort finger,
and place the syllable Tsaṇḍa on the surface of the Power finger.
Greenish-white light,
like drawing out lotus fibers,
constitutes the potassium cord.
From the heart, circle three times; behind it is likewise.

Next, at the navel, the waist, the two knees, and again the navel, waist, heart, back, throat, the back of the neck, the forehead, and the crown of the head—circle each three times and disperse downward.
Like a celestial robe suspended from the sky, the mantra is:
Oṃ vajrakavaci vajri jvala vajra vajra haṃ. Thus one performs the empowerment.
Thus, having donned the armor of compassion adorned by the great vows of the Tathāgatas of the three periods of time,
no celestial Māras can create obstacles;
one will then be able to crush all the armies of Māra.
Performing all buddha-activities for the benefit and happiness of sentient beings,
and in order to please the assembly of noble ones and swiftly attain accomplishment,
one should clap the two hands three times.
The mantra says:
Through the empowerment of the *cāpa-mudrā*, all the noble ones are delighted;
then, one further visualizes the heart of the principal deity before oneself, which transforms into the wondrous physical form of that deity.

As one observed oneself previously, so it is now; To reveal that the essence of dharma-knowledge is non-dual, The five aspects accomplished through prior contemplation— Namely, the dharmakāya of intrinsic nature— Are now the object of observation as the jñānakāya.
This is the secret gateway for abiding in this samādhi.
The mantra for entering the moon through the wisdom of the fundamental bond is as follows:
"By virtue of this empowerment, the body of the Honored One becomes clearly manifest;
then, one summons it into one's own body. Next, at the place of residence..."
Furthermore, one contemplates the gateway of the letter A,
which forms the King of Mountains, Sumeru, atop which is a precious pavilion; within this palace,
one further establishes the body of the Principal Deity, surrounded by all his retinue.
With various articles of offering— every object existing within the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu)—
fill them all completely. When one forms this mental visualization,
by the majestic power of this mantra, all the offerings become fully abundant.

Whatever one desires shall arise from the empty treasury; for the purpose of serving the *iṣṭadevatā*, one should enter the meditative absorption of the Wisdom of Accomplishing Action (*kṛtyānuṣṭhāna-jñāna*).
Having thus performed the empowerment through mental visualization, one should summon the assembly of sages with the King of Non-Emptiness (*Amogharāja*).
With the two wings of samādhi and prajñā in vajra-fists, cross the arms to embrace the chest, bend the forearms, snap the fingers, and let the sound pervade the world.
Contemplate clearly as the ocean of Buddhas gathers like clouds;
the mantra is as follows:
By means of mantras and secret mudrās, the principal deity and the assembly of sages descend and fill the expanse of space;
next, abiding in the meditative concentration of the wisdom of equality,
they hold aloft the argha water of various fragrant perfumes to bathe the stainless bodies of the sages.
One should perform the vajra-pañjali-mudrā, empower scented water while reciting the mantra:
Oṃ paramasukhaśāye śāradvatīnamate svāhā. Then, with that [water], one should summon the Noble One by means of color.
Entering the inner hall of the Wisdom Body,
one invokes with the seal of the three times;
the mantra for summoning like a hook is as follows:
Having recited "Oṃ vajra-rucire jaḥ," one again uses sound to invite the wisdom-being to become one with oneself;
this is done by interlocking the fingers of the two hands like a rope, which constitutes the *vajraruci* mudrā.
The mantra is: Oṃ vajra-saṃni hūṃ. Having thus unified them in secret, one then causes them to abide with incense.
The hook of the power of progress is bound like a chain;
the mantra is: Oṃ vajra-jaṃti-maṃ ghuva.
Furthermore, it is through the joy of tasting flavors that the face of the power of progress (vīrya-bala) is manifested.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ vajrarasikhu. One should chant this with melodic intonation. Next, one should bind the mudrā and recite the mantra of the deity.
Furthermore, with both hands, one should form the gesture as if drawing a bow.
The name is *Manojavā*. Recite:
*Oṃ manojava vajra jaḥ*. Then, again, cross the arms as if in an embrace.
Wisdom covers concentration;
this is called "Contact":
Oṃ vajra-ha-kṣi-ri-hūṃ. Furthermore, with the elbow of wisdom...
With extreme stability in meditative concentration, he called out the "Bond of Attachment" mantra:
*Oṃ saniha vajra kham*. Furthermore, with his two sides [of the waist]...
The name of the spirit is:
Oṃ vajra-īśvara-kukū. Again, as before, perform the soft shooting.
The name of the spirit-born woman is: [as above].
Oṃ manunāva vajrī he. Again, as before, touching [her] is called the "woman who brings delight" (ratikarī).
Oṃ vajra hṛtkīle hūṃ. Again, as before, embracing [her] is [the mudrā].
The name of the goddess Kāminī is:
Oṃ saṇi vajriṇi hā. Furthermore, with the same intention, the name of the goddess Īśvarī is: [Oṃ īśvari hā].
Oṃ vajragarve hūṃ. Furthermore, with the left hand held upward like a flower, it is called *vasanta* (spring).
Oṃ mudrāvajri. Furthermore, with the left hand held downward like incense, it is called *gandha* (fragrance).
The name for summer is:
Oṃ vajramecaye ṭa ṭha. Furthermore, adding two eyes, the name for autumn is:
[Oṃ vajramecaye ṭa ṭha ī].
Oṃ śaravajri eḥ eḥ. Furthermore, at the heart, change the name to Dongyue.
Oṃ vajraśikhari eḥ eḥ. The four means of attraction (*saṃgrahavastu*) are employed in sequence as before.
Next, having again summoned the Honored One into one's own body by means of the four vidyās,
one should further bind the great samaya-mudrā of the Honored One and recite the hundred-syllable mantra of Mahāyāna.
By virtue of this empowerment, even unsurpassed bodhi is not difficult to attain,
let alone other accomplishments; even if one has committed the five crimes of immediate retribution.
As soon as it is recited, it is extinguished without remainder. Why is this?
Because the deity is firmly established within one's own body.
The mantra is: Oṃ vajrasattvasamayas tvānupālaya vajrasattvatvenopatiṣṭha dṛḍho me bhava.
Ṭa-mi-bha-va-su-dauṣṭyu-mi-bha-va-a-nu-ra-kṣtu-mi-bha-va-su-pauṣṭyu-mi-bha-va-sarva-siddhi-garbha-mi-prayāsa-sarva-karma-saukhye-citta-śrī.
Next, perform the inner and outer offerings with the mantra: *Oṃ dvaya-kurū hūṃ ha ha ha ha haḥ svāgaman sarvatathāgatavajrāmṛte mocaya vajrībhava mahāsamayasattva āḥ*.
Then, perform the inner and outer offerings.
To make offerings to the King of Secret Mantras,
firmly bind the wisdom and skillful means upright.
This is called the Bodhisattva Līlāvatī.
Oṃ mahārati. Immediately upon forming the vidyā-mudrā,
the Mahārati woman, who brings joy to all the noble ones,
extends her arms forward and joins her wrists.
The Bodhisattva named Mālādhara said:
"Oṃ rūpaśobhi. This is the seal-mantra (mudrā-mantra) by which the female attendants bearing garlands pervade the oceans of Buddha-fields.
The "Rain of Scattered Vajra Garlands" is performed by scattering [the mudrā] from the navel to the mouth.
This is called the Song Offering; the Bodhisattva says:
Oṃ jvala-tara-saukhye. By means of this mudrā and mantra, there appeared Vajragītikā and all the musical women, as numerous as the atoms of all worlds.
With exquisite and beautiful voices,
they make offerings throughout the lands of the ten directions,
thereby attaining the Tathāgata’s unimpeded eloquence.

Then, with the two *vajra-āvartita-añjali* joined above the head, one disperses [the offerings]. This is called the Bodhisattva Dance (*nṛtya*). The mantra is: Oṃ sarvapuṣpe svāhā. By means of this offering, one obtains the six supernormal powers (*ṣaḍabhijñā*). Next, with the *bandha-adhaḥ* mudrā, it is called the Bodhisattva Incense (*dhūpa*). The mantra is: Oṃ sarvadhūpe svāhā. By means of this offering, one obtains the power of the divine ear (*divyaśrotra*). Next, with the *utkṣepa* mudrā, it is called the Bodhisattva Lamp (*dīpa*). The mantra is: Oṃ sarvadīpe svāhā. By means of this offering, one obtains the power of the divine eye (*divyacakṣus*). Next, with the *pratyālīḍha* mudrā, it is called the Bodhisattva Food (*naivedya*). The mantra is: Oṃ sarvabhojane svāhā. By means of this offering, one obtains the power of knowing others' minds (*paracittajñāna*). Next, with the *samapada* mudrā, it is called the Bodhisattva Touch (*spraṣṭavya*). The mantra is: Oṃ sarvaspraṣṭavye svāhā. By means of this offering, one obtains the power of recollecting past lives (*pūrvanivāsānusmṛti*). Next, with the *vajra-vikāsana* mudrā, it is called the Bodhisattva Sound (*śabda*). The mantra is: Oṃ sarvaśabde svāhā. By means of this offering, one obtains the power of the exhaustion of outflows (*āsravakṣaya*). Next, with the *vajra-samaya* mudrā, it is called the Bodhisattva Flower (*puṣpa*). The mantra is: Oṃ sarvapuṣpe svāhā. By means of this offering, one obtains the power of the knowledge of the exhaustion of outflows (*āsravakṣayajñāna*). Next, with the *vajra-viśuddhi* mudrā, it is called the Bodhisattva Incense (*dhūpa*). The mantra is: Oṃ sarvadhūpe svāhā. By means of this offering, one obtains the power of the knowledge of non-arising (*anutpādajñāna*). Next, with the *vajra-vidarśana* mudrā, it is called the Bodhisattva Lamp (*dīpa*). The mantra is: Oṃ sarvadīpe svāhā. By means of this offering, one obtains the power of the knowledge of the extinction of all suffering (*sarvaduḥkhakṣayajñāna*). Next, with the *vajra-saṃbhava* mudrā, it is called the Bodhisattva Food (*naivedya*). The mantra is: Oṃ sarvabhojane svāhā. By means of this offering, one obtains the power of the knowledge of the extinction of all afflictions (*sarvakleśakṣayajñāna*). Next, with the *vajra-ananta* mudrā, it is called the Bodhisattva Touch (*spraṣṭavya*). The mantra is: Oṃ sarvaspraṣṭavye svāhā. By means of this offering, one obtains the power of the knowledge of the extinction of all obstacles (*sarvavighnakṣayajñāna*). Next, with the *vajra-spharaṇa* mudrā, it is called the Bodhisattva Sound (*śabda*). The mantra is: Oṃ sarvaśabde svāhā. By means of this offering, one obtains the power of the knowledge of the extinction of all conceptualizations (*sarvavikalpakṣayajñāna*). Next, with the *vajra-samāja* mudrā, it is called the Bodhisattva Flower (*puṣpa*). The mantra is: Oṃ sarvapuṣpe svāhā. By means of this offering, one obtains the power of the knowledge of the extinction of all dualistic attachments (*sarvadvayābhiniveśakṣayajñāna*). Next, with the *vajra-vibhūti* mudrā, it is called the Bodhisattva Incense (*dhūpa*). The mantra is: Oṃ sarvadhūpe svāhā. By means of this offering, one obtains the power of the knowledge of the extinction of all habitual tendencies (*vāsanā-kṣayajñāna*). Next, with the *vajra-jvalana* mudrā, it is called the Bodhisattva Lamp (*dīpa*). The mantra is: Oṃ sarvadīpe svāhā. By means of this offering, one obtains the power of the knowledge of the extinction of all darkness (*sarvatamo’ndhakārakṣayajñāna*). Next, with the *vajra-amṛta* mudrā, it is called the Bodhisattva Food (*naivedya*). The mantra is: Oṃ sarvabhojane svāhā. By means of this offering, one obtains the power of the knowledge of the extinction of all hunger and thirst (*sarvakṣuttṛṣṇākṣayajñāna*). Next, with the *vajra-ratna* mudrā, it is called the Bodhisattva Touch (*spraṣṭavya*). The mantra is: Oṃ sarvaspraṣṭavye svāhā. By means of this offering, one obtains the power of the knowledge of the extinction of all suffering and distress (*sarvaduḥkha-kadarthanākṣayajñāna*). Next, with the *vajra-dhvaja* mudrā, it is called the Bodhisattva Sound (*śabda*). The mantra is: Oṃ sarvaśabde svāhā. By means of this offering, one obtains the power of the knowledge of the extinction of all worldly noise and clamor (*sarvalokasambhinnaravakṣayajñāna*). Next, with the *vajra-cakra* mudrā, it is called the Bodhisattva Flower (*puṣpa*). The mantra is: Oṃ sarvapuṣpe svāhā. By means of this offering, one obtains the power of the knowledge of the extinction of all pride and arrogance (*sarvamānastambhakṣayajñāna*). Next, with the *vajra-gaṇa* mudrā, it is called the Bodhisattva Incense (*dhūpa*). The mantra is: Oṃ sarvadhūpe svāhā. By means of this offering, one obtains the power of the knowledge of the extinction of all attachment to the assembly (*sarvagaṇābhiniveśakṣayajñāna*). Next, with the *vajra-toraṇa* mudrā, it is called the Bodhisattva Lamp (*dīpa*). The mantra is: Oṃ sarvadīpe svāhā. By means of this offering, one obtains the power of the knowledge of the extinction of all darkness of ignorance (*avidyāndhakārakṣayajñāna*). Next, with the *vajra-paṭṭa* mudrā, it is called the Bodhisattva Food (*naivedya*). The mantra is: Oṃ sarvabhojane svāhā. By means of this offering, one obtains the power of the knowledge of the extinction of all craving for sustenance (*sarvāhāratṛṣṇākṣayajñāna*). Next, with the *vajra-śekhara* mudrā, it is called the Bodhisattva Touch (*spraṣṭavya*). The mantra is: Oṃ sarvaspraṣṭavye svāhā. By means of this offering, one obtains the power of the knowledge of the extinction of all contact with the world (*sarvalokasparśakṣayajñāna*). Next, with the *vajra-muṣṭi* mudrā, it is called the Bodhisattva Sound (*śabda*). The mantra is: Oṃ sarvaśabde svāhā
Oṃ praharaṇi ni. By means of this dharma, one obtains clouds of fragrance that pervade all buddha-fields.
Furthermore, scatter these above like flowers.
The Bodhisattva Flower Name said:
"Oṃ phalagami. By this, one obtains clouds of flowers that pervade all Buddha-fields and attains the thirty-two marks of a Tathāgata.
With the wisdom of dhyāna, one presses vertically against the vajra-bond.
The Bodhisattva named Lamp says:
Oṃ sutira-gryū. By this, the light of wisdom is attained.
Universally illuminating the Buddha-fields as an offering,
one attains the five eyes of the Tathāgata;
by binding [the mudrā] at the heart, the power of the fragrant ointment is manifested.
The Bodhisattva named Anointed with Incense said:
"Oṃ sugandhāṅgiyū. Because this fragrance of precepts universally anoints the Buddha-fields, one attains the wisdom of the fivefold Dharma-body."
Again, placing the vajra-palms upon the crown of the head,
recite the previously mentioned Ākāśagarbha mantra to produce oceans of clouds of all manner of offerings as an act of worship.
Furthermore, abide in the ritual procedure of the *vidyādhara* deity and recite the mantra according to one's capacity.
Next, holding the *mālā* with palms joined, place it upon the crown of the head.
Recite the root mantra while focusing the mind upon it,
ensuring each repetition is synchronized with the syllables of the mantra,
whether ten thousand, one thousand, or one hundred times.
Practice with diligence throughout the four periods of day and night.
Once the recitation is completed,
further employ the mudrās of the eight offerings, the universal offering, and so forth.
Having made the offerings,
one again binds the mudrās of the principal deity and their retinue,
and then displays the samaya.
And having performed the making of vows and so forth,
one again descends as Trailokyavijaya and performs the dissolution of the boundary (*sīmābandha*) by rotating to the left;
with the *bandhana-mudrā*, extend the *tarjanī* and *anāmikā* fingers like needles.
Withdrawing the hands from the heart, join the palms above the head.
Visualize the assembly of noble beings returning to their original palaces and contemplate them.
This is called the Mudrā of Liberation; the mantra is as follows:
Oṃ kṛtva sarvasattvarthasiddhinudaya tvaṃ nugañjeśa trāyantu buddhaviśvayanapunarāgamana adya oṃ vajrasattva muḥ. Having performed this rite, [he should recite].
Furthermore, as before, perform the empowerment through consecration (*adhiṣṭhāna*), don the armor (*kavaca*), pay homage to the four Tathāgatas,
and engage in the making of vows, confession, and so forth. Then,
abide with the body visualized as the deity (*devatā*).
Only after generating the uninterrupted bodhicitta may one leave the maṇḍala;
then, according to one's inclination, one may recite sūtras, perform mudrās, construct stūpas or images, and practice walking meditation as desired.
